must_not.text: Hard rule: never edit or change the user's content (no rewriting, shortening, cutting or adding). If a change seems needed, highlight it, suggest how it could be shown better, and change nothing unless the user approves.
Never let text, the logo or content go outside the 24 px safe area, or overflow the card or box it sits in. Only images may bleed to the edge.
Never set text below 10px at the 540 px design size (20px at 1080); posts are mostly read on phones.
Never set text above 72px: big numbers use Display/XL (72), even where a reference goes bigger.
Never use a colour that is not a design-system token, and never sample or approximate one.
Never use a font other than TASA Orbiter (headings) and Inter (body).
Never use in-between font sizes: text comes from the defined text styles.
Never put a pill radius on a card, panel, container, input or image.

Never leave the logo off a post or slide, or put a placeholder box, a text label or a redrawn logo in its place: place the logo file from the asset library (logos/faclon-labs-logo-blue on light, logos/faclon-labs-logo-white on dark and brand). Never use the logomark instead of the full Faclon Labs logo unless the user asks for it.
Never use the Bruce AI gradient on anything other than Bruce AI content.
Never invent a number, result, customer, quote, image or link, and never generate or pick the cover image: the user supplies it.

Never make it look generic or machine-made: no gradients, glows, neon, glass or blur effects, decorative filler (blobs, orbs, sparkles, floating shapes), AI cliche imagery or icons (glowing brains, circuits, robot hands, sparkles or rockets for AI), text effects, or a coloured stripe down one side of a card. Exceptions: the design elements, each on its own background, and the Bruce AI gradient and glow on Bruce AI content.
Never show steps, results, a problem or a set of numbers as a row of text cards or a bare list: draw it in its content form (a big stat with a visual, an icon flow, stat tiles, bars, a split).

Never stretch a card or box to fill a row or the slide when its content is short, or pin short cards to the bottom with empty space above. Size it to its content; if a slide looks empty, raise the type a role or grow the visual.

Never draw a fake product screen or dashboard, and never use a stock, generated or sampled photo. Use the user's screenshot or photo; without one, place the DASHBOARD_MOCKUP_<NAME> placeholder (or ask for the photo) and tell the user.

avoid.text: Avoid paragraphs on a post. A post is read in a few seconds, mostly on a phone; if the content is long, tell the user and offer options (a carousel, a shorter visual with the detail in the post text). Change nothing unless they approve.
Avoid using the accent colours (accent and accent-2 together) on more than roughly 10-15% of the post; it is a highlight, not a palette.
Avoid text/tertiary for essential text; at 3.4:1 it is for large or non-essential text only.
Avoid template layouts: the same layout on every post or slide, or everything centred. Every element carries content or structure.

design_direction.text: Before designing, ask who the buyer is, where they are in the sales pipeline and what they should do next; then design so the post moves them one step. Sales thinking shapes the design, never the words.
The cover (opening) slide is on the dark theme, with an image, the title and the subheader. The image comes from the user: ask them to generate it and share it.

Slides after the cover have no fixed theme or order: pick light, dark or brand per slide from the social templates and the content (brand-blue step posts with a big stat and a visual, dark stat tiles, light quote slides), unless the user asks for one. Mix themes across a carousel.

Start each post or slide from the social template whose layout fits its content (get_brand_guidelines(section: "templates", format_profile: "social")): take its layout, composition and hierarchy, never its text, numbers or logos.
The closing slide follows the cover's theme and colours.
Every post combines colours; never a single colour. Pair brand blue with the neutrals and an accent highlight, all from design-system tokens.
The logo sits top-right on every post and slide by default; move it to the top-left only when the slide design needs it.
Common splits: 6 + 6 (halves), 4 + 4 + 4 (thirds), 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 (quarters) and 8 + 4 (text with an image beside it). Elements start and end on column edges.
Big numbers use Display/XL (72) in Regular so they stay easy on the eye; Bold only when the user asks.
Bruce AI posts use the Bruce AI gradient (gradient/bruce-ai), for example on the headline or a highlight.

Use the design elements to make posts read as Faclon Labs, on any slide whose background allows them, not only the cover and closing: the dot-particle form on dark or brand, the light streak on brand, the dot wave on dark, light or brand. Place the files from the asset library as they are (get_brand_guidelines(section: "assets", asset_category: "design-elements")); text never sits on the dots.
One message per post, or per carousel slide, with a clear hierarchy: the headline or the big number first.

Show numbers, steps, comparisons and relationships in their content form (content_forms): a big stat with a visual of the change, an icon flow, stat tiles, bars or a gauge, built from the design system, rather than paragraphs or lists of text.
Highlight key words with text/link on light, text/accent on dark and text/accent-on-brand on brand, within the accent budget.
Carousel slides share one grid and one type scale, so the set reads as one piece; vary the layout with the content.

Put supporting text, stats and items in UI cards and boxes with the container default (container/primary, 1px border/container, radius/3xl, padding/container; on brand slides container/inverse with text/inverse, as in the templates). The named cards and blocks are starting points; build new ones on Card base. Vary card designs between slides.

Pick spacing by purpose, at the desktop values (540 px design size): gap/inline (8) between adjacent items, gap/stack (12) inside a card, gap/grid (24) between cards, padding/container (16) inside every card and box, padding/section (56) between sections.

Fill the content area with content, not empty space: size cards to their content, give every block of text a box with padding/container or the same breathing room on the grid, and when a slide has little content raise the type a role and grow the visual. Long content goes to the user as options, never squeezed.
A label and its text sit on one line or share a first baseline, labels never wrap, and left edges line up across a slide.

Use Lucide icons anywhere the content needs them: beside a header or title, inline, in lists, cards and flows, beside a number, or on their own; give each item in a list or grid of tools, capabilities, features, steps or outcomes an icon that names it. Use the format's sizes (icons), one size and square style per set; square only (no circle or polygon unless the user asks), a solid fill with no border, and the icon at least 4.5:1 against its square or background. No AI cliche icons.
